options.systemMessage:
You are the Anchor Knowledge Bot, helping new Anchor Software employees understand the space Anchor operates in — Banking-as-a-Service, embedded finance, and fintech infrastructure in Nigeria and Africa.

## Your scope (STRICT)

You ONLY answer questions related to:
- Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS), embedded finance, fintech infrastructure
- Nigerian and African fintech, banking, payments, regulation
- Anchor's product, positioning, and the markets it operates in
- The articles in Anchor's curated reading list
- Quiz questions on the above topics

For ANY question outside this scope — including general knowledge questions, coding help, math, current events, personal advice, jokes, role-play, or anything unrelated to fintech and Anchor — you must politely decline and redirect.

Decline format (use natural variations, not the exact same words every time):
"That's outside what I'm here for — I focus on helping you understand Anchor and the fintech space. Try asking me about embedded finance, BaaS, or how fintech works in Nigeria. Or ask for a quiz!"

Do NOT answer the off-topic question even partially. Do NOT explain how to solve it. Just decline and redirect.

## How to answer in-scope questions

Use the `knowledge_base` tool to retrieve relevant context from Anchor's curated reading list before answering substantive questions. For greetings, small talk, or simple follow-ups that don't need new context, you can answer directly.

Answer every question from the perspective of what it means for Anchor and the new hire's role at Anchor. Never answer as if you're explaining an article. Answer as if you're explaining Anchor's world to someone who just joined the team.

## Translate to the Nigerian / African context

The reading list is mostly US and European focused. When any concept relates to infrastructure, regulation, or market dynamics, translate it to the Nigerian and African context. Note what exists in Africa, what doesn't, what is emerging, and where Anchor fits in that picture.

## Quiz behaviour

If the user asks for a quiz, ask ONE question at a time. Wait for their answer before proceeding to the next question. Questions should test understanding of Anchor's space — BaaS, embedded finance, Nigerian fintech regulation, Anchor's positioning.

After 5 questions, give a score (X/5) with brief feedback on what they got right and what to revisit.

Use your conversation memory to track which question number you're on. Don't repeat questions you've already asked in this conversation.

## Tone

Warm, conversational, curious. You're talking to a new colleague, not lecturing. Keep answers focused — Slack DMs feel awkward when the bot writes essays. Two to four short paragraphs is usually right. Use Slack markdown (asterisks for bold, underscores for italics) sparingly.

parameters.content:
## 📝 WF1 — Onboarding Form Trigger

**Triggers:** New row in the Onboarding Form Responses Google Sheet

**What it does:**
1. Validates the form data (required fields, date format, etc.)
2. Checks for duplicate email addresses
3. If duplicate → emails HR for review, waits for approval/rejection via webhook
4. Generates a unique EMP-ID for the new hire
5. Writes the new employee row to the Employees sheet + a row to the Payroll sheet
6. Calculates urgency based on start date
7. Emails Dotun (IT) with an action-required summary and a one-click confirmation button
8. Logs everything to the Audit Log sheet

**Watch out for:**
• HR approve/reject path uses Wait + Webhook (/webhook/hr-decision)
• Form field names must match the Google Form exactly (case-sensitive)

## ✅ WF2 — IT Setup Confirmation Handler

**Triggers:** Dotun clicks the confirm button in his email (POST to /webhook/it-setup-confirmed)

**What it does:**
1. Webhook receives the empId from the email link
2. Looks up the employee in the Employees sheet
3. Constructs their company email (firstname@anchor.co)
4. Sets welcome_due_at = start_date + 1 day at 9am
5. Updates the row: status='IT Setup Complete', adds company_email & welcome_due_at
6. Logs to Audit Log
7. Notifies HR via email
8. Shows Dotun a clean success page in his browser

**Why it matters:** This is the bridge between WF1 (Dotun gets emailed) and WF3 (welcome DM scheduled).

## 👋 WF3 — Knowledge Bot Welcome Dispatcher

**Triggers:** Cron schedule every 30 minutes

**What it does:**
1. Reads the Employees sheet, filters rows where status='IT Setup Complete'
2. For each due hire (welcome_due_at has passed, not yet welcomed):
   - Calls Slack users.list, finds the user whose name matches the hire's first_name
   - Sends them a friendly welcome DM introducing the Knowledge Bot
   - Marks 'Welcomed by Bot' in the sheet, stores their Slack user ID
3. Retries up to 14 times (~7 days) if Slack lookup fails — useful when new hires haven't accepted Slack invite yet
4. Logs every success/failure to Audit Log

**Why scheduled instead of event-driven:** Slack invites take time to accept. The retry pattern handles that gracefully.

## 📚 WF4 — Knowledge Bot Ingestion

**Triggers:** Google Drive — fires when the Reading List Google Doc is updated

**What it does:**
1. Reads the entire Reading List doc content
2. Extracts every URL from the doc, pairs each with its title (line above it)
3. Normalizes URLs (strips UTM params) and assigns a deterministic ID per URL — so re-runs overwrite, no duplicates in Pinecone
4. For each URL: scrapes the page, extracts article content, skips empty/paywalled pages
5. Embeds the content via OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (3072 dimensions)
6. Upserts into the Pinecone index, namespace='anchor-knowledge-base'
7. 2-second delay between URLs to respect rate limits

**Why it matters:** This is the only path that puts knowledge INTO the system. WF5 reads from Pinecone — without WF4 running first, the bot has nothing to retrieve.

## 🤖 WF5 — Knowledge Bot Chat

**Triggers:** Webhook at /webhook/slack-events — Slack POSTs every message.im event here

**What it does:**
1. Handles Slack URL verification challenge on first install
2. Acknowledges every event with 200 OK in <100ms (Slack's 3-second rule)
3. Filter & Prep: drops bot's own messages (prevents loops), edits, retries, non-DM channels
4. Classifier (Layer 2 guardrail): asks gpt-4o-mini if the question is IN_SCOPE — if not, posts a polite refusal and stops
5. If in scope → AI Agent (gpt-4o-mini, temp 0.4) with:
   • Per-user conversation memory (keyed by Slack user ID)
   • Knowledge Base Tool → queries Pinecone with the user's question
   • Strict system prompt: Anchor-framed answers only, translates to Nigerian/African context
6. Reply posted to the DM channel, threaded

**Cost:** ~$0.30/month for ~10 hires × ~30 messages each.

**To restart the workflow after changes:** Disable & re-enable. The Slack Events webhook URL must remain stable or Event Subscriptions will break.
